A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same APOLLO work, with readable text, tables, figures, algorithms, and appendices. The original proof examples are retained; v3 Appendices B–C become v4 Appendices F–G.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original APOLLO experiments on miniF2F, including accuracy, computational budgets, proof-length distributions, and recursion-depth analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds PutnamBench and ProofNet evaluations, component ablations, alternative repair/search comparisons, and computational analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same syntax refinement, Sorrifier, automated solving, recursive sub-proof generation, and assembly procedure. The ablation's LLM Re-invoker names the existing recursive prompting component.

E1.justification: v3 evaluates miniF2F competition problems. v4 additionally evaluates 658 PutnamBench problems (Table 3) and ProofNet undergraduate mathematics (Table 7), substantially expanding the mathematical evaluation coverage. Both benchmarks were merely cited in v3.

E2.justification: v4 adds direct comparisons against o3-mini with REPL-feedback repair (Table 8) and Kimina-7B with RMaxTS (Table 9). These introduce relevant alternative repair and search strategies. Table 2 retains its comparator membership despite abbreviated method names.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include eight component combinations, REPL-feedback budgets of 5 and 10 attempts, RMaxTS sampling at 4×128, and maximum/average cost accounting over all problems versus Apollo-assisted subsets. The original miniF2F split, Lean version, and default top-32 sampling remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 adds controlled ablations of Syntax Refiner, AutoSolver, and recursive LLM prompting on two models. Appendix E measures module activation across four models, while Appendix B examines cost-accounting subsets. The existing proof-length, recursion-depth, and illustrative repair analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-experiment counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new checklist explains the existing multiple-attempt proof evaluation practice without adding an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their original scores. New results include PutnamBench's 11/658 proofs for Apollo at 108 samples versus 10/658 for Kimina at 192, and ProofNet's 18.3% versus 11.3% at respective budgets of 96 and 128. Tables 4–6 and 8–10 add ablation, comparator, cost, and module-activation results. These are additional comparisons, not same-setting v3-to-v4 performance gains.

T1.justification: No new theoretical results, assumptions, derivations, or mathematical proofs are introduced. Algorithm 1, the proof-length definition, and the formal proof examples are retained. The added budget analyses are empirical.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the model-size scope of its SOTA claim from 7B-or-less to 8B-or-less, and the abstract qualifies SOTA as of August 2025. The conclusion extends its claimed one-to-two-order budget reduction to tokens as well as samples. The central compiler-guided repair contribution remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations of component interactions, argues for reporting costs on Apollo-assisted problems, identifies GPU generation as the computational bottleneck, and describes REPL feedback as complementary. The original proof-length/depth interpretations and limitations concerning sketch quality and tree-search integration remain.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D add the REPL-feedback prompt, a five-minute compilation timeout, a 16,384-token context window, and verification/generation timings. These are newly documented details, without evidence that existing experiment settings changed. The original implementation description, hardware setup, and code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix C expands positioning relative to REPL-feedback repair and RMaxTS, including proposed complementarity with feedback-based approaches. Section 2 is substantially unchanged. Reference 45 duplicates the DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5 work already cited as reference 30 rather than introducing a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. Changes include local terminology and explanation edits, author/contact formatting, acknowledgments, a NeurIPS checklist, and new experimental subsections and appendices. Existing appendix discussions are renumbered rather than rewritten extensively.

P2.justification: v4 adds eight tables and substantially reformats the document into the NeurIPS layout. Existing tables are reformatted, Figure 4's three model panels become one horizontal row, and proof figures are resized and repositioned, sometimes sharing a page. Existing figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: The controlled ablations and direct REPL-feedback/RMaxTS comparisons address important gaps in v3's evidence about component contributions and alternative repair strategies. PutnamBench and ProofNet also test applicability beyond miniF2F. These substantial validation gains outweigh localized reporting defects, although efficiency claims need correction: Tables 5–6 list Kimina's maximum token budget as 1.3M below its 1.6M mean, and Table 6 reports both Kimina averages as 1.6M despite Appendix B claiming consistent savings.
